title: Cell Division
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Cell Division Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: The role of the cell cycle and mitosis in growth and repair; chromosomes in the nucleus; the function of stem cells in embryos, in adult animals and in the meristems of plants; the use of stem cells in medicine and agriculture, including therapeutic cloning, and the potential benefits and risks.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on cell division: chromosomes, the cell cycle and mitosis, differentiation, stem cells, meristems and therapeutic cloning. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Stem cells can divide and differentiate into many types of cell.
body_html:
How to think about it

Cells divide by mitosis for growth and repair.

  • Before dividing, the cell grows and copies its chromosomes. Mitosis then makes two genetically identical daughter cells.
  • Stem cells are undifferentiated: embryonic stem cells can become almost any cell; adult stem cells only some; plant meristems any plant cell.
  • Stem cells may treat diseases such as diabetes, but there are risks and ethical issues.
Example

46 chromosomes divide by mitosis. Each daughter cell?

Identical copies

Answer: 46

Example

Which stem cells can become almost any cell?

From embryos

Answer: embryonic stem cells

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mitosis makes sex cells.
  • Thinking daughter cells have half the chromosomes.
  • Thinking adult stem cells can become any cell.

faq.a: Cell division that makes two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. It is used for growth and repair.
Undifferentiated cells that can divide and become specialised cells. Embryonic stem cells can become almost any cell; adult and plant meristem stem cells have narrower or plant-only uses.
Making an embryo with the patient's own genes. Its stem cells could treat the patient without being rejected by the immune system.

items.q: A human cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 46 = 92.

items.q: A garden onion cell has 16 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 16 × 2 = 32.

items.q: A human cell has 46 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 46 × 2 = 92.

items.q: What happens before a cell divides by mitosis?
c: It grows, copies its DNA and makes more sub-cellular structures such as ribosomes and mitochondria.
items.e: The cell cycle.

items.q: How many chromosomes are in a human body cell?
items.e: Half from each parent.

items.q: How do the daughter cells made by mitosis compare with the parent cell?
c: They are genetically identical, with the same number of chromosomes.
items.e: Clones.
